subject: Epsilon Systems — interconnect options: VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@epsilonsys.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Epsilon Systems — interconnect options: VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As we scope the private deployment for Epsilon Systems, we'd like to align on the connectivity approach before the pilot starts. High-level options are: VPC Peering (direct VPC-to-VPC path), AWS PrivateLink (endpoint service), or Site-to-Site VPN (IPSec tunnel).

Can you confirm the following from your side so we can finalize the recommendation and SOW:
- Which AWS accounts/VPCs will host your inference clients? (CIDR ranges)
- Do you have a preference for carrier-managed cross-connects (Direct Connect) vs encrypted internet tunnels for the pilot?
- Any constraints around egress IPs or firewall/NAT?

We see three trade buckets: latency/throughput, per-connection operational complexity, and security/compliance (auditability, traffic flow visibility). I'll loop in Marcus for an architecture sketch after we get your details.

Attached: short diagram showing the three patterns and our rough latency expectations.

Next steps: if you can share the VPC CIDRs and whether you want a single shared VPC or per-team VPCs, we'll produce a recommended path plus a minimal-change pilot plan.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]
[Attachment: redwood_network_diagram_v2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@epsilonsys.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Epsilon Systems — interconnect options: VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. A couple quick answers:
- We will start with a single shared VPC in our prod-account (10.10.0.0/16).
- Pilot traffic will originate from our inference-clients subnet (10.10.10.0/24).
- We prefer to avoid exposing additional public IPs; our security team likes endpoint-based models.

Given that, our security lead suggested PrivateLink for the pilot because it avoids route table changes and keeps traffic within the AWS fabric. However, they are concerned about throughput caps and cross-account endpoint scaling.

Would appreciate a short list of operational pros/cons and any throughput numbers you can share. Also fine if you propose a hybrid approach (e.g., PrivateLink for control-plane; peering for high-volume inference).

Thanks —
Alice Tan
Head of Cloud Ops, Epsilon Systems
alice.tan@epsilonsys.com

Jordan / Kimberly —

Quick internal note after reading Alice's reply and reviewing Epsilon's constraints:

Summary of recommended posture for the pilot (concise):
- Primary: PrivateLink (endpoint service) for ingress from Epsilon's shared VPC to Redwood's private deploy. Rationale: security team requirement (no route table changes), predictable auth via endpoint policies, simpler audit trail.
- Secondary (fallback/high-throughput): Dedicated VPC peering as a canary path for heavy-burst inference if PrivateLink throughput becomes limiting. Rationale: lower per-packet overhead, higher sustained throughput and smaller tail latency.
- Not recommended for the pilot: Site-to-Site VPN as the only path. Use only as a temporary fallback if customer cannot configure endpoint services. VPN increases jitter and complicates NAT/firewall behavior.

Operational bullets we should include in the SOW:
- Work with Epsilon's netops to create an endpoint service in Redwood Prod VPCs (we host the service behind NLBs with fixed ENIs).
- Document per-connection throughput ceilings (we'll load-test with their traffic shape; attach CSV with numbers).
- Define a canary peering window: if observed 99th percentile P95 token latency crosses X ms at sustained RPS Y, open peering and migrate heavy clients.
- Rollout plan and rollback steps (how we revoke endpoints / remove peering).

I attached a quick CSV with observed PrivateLink vs Peering baseline for our standard model at different sequence lengths — useful as a starting point for SOW numbers.

Marcus
Principal Infra Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: privatelink-vs-peering-latency-table.csv]

Subject: RE: Epsilon Systems — interconnect options: VPC peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Alice —

Thanks for the quick details. Based on your constraints and our internal validation, here's a concise recommended pilot plan (we've kept it low-friction for your security team):

Pilot recommendation (summary):
- Stage 1 (0–2 weeks): Configure AWS PrivateLink endpoint from Epsilon's shared VPC (10.10.0.0/16) to Redwood's endpoint-service in our Prod VPC. We will provide the endpoint service name, policies, and the NLB configuration.
- Stage 2 (1–3 weeks): Run traffic ramp and load tests with a controlled client subset (10–20% of inference traffic). Monitor throughput and P95 token latency closely.
- Stage 3 (conditional): If sustained throughput exceeds the PrivateLink observed ceiling for your workload, we will provision a dedicated VPC peering connection and migrate high-throughput clients. Peering will be announced in the SOW as an escalation path (no production cutover until jointly authorized).

Operational considerations we will document in the SOW:
- Security: all connections authenticated via TLS and endpoint policies; we will provide audit logs for connection establishment and auth events.
- Networking: we will share exact NLB IPs and recommend security-group rules; no internet-facing IPs required from your side.
- Support: 2x weekly sync during pilot + on-call handoff for peering cutover.

Next steps: I attached a draft SOW with names and milestone dates (sow-draft-epsilonsys.docx) and the diagram/latency CSV for your review. If this approach looks good, can we schedule a 30-minute netops alignment call on Wednesday?

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
